mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES recovers from near-flat to less negative levels after the latest dip, weekday foot traffic and adjacent discretionary spending will lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying above its t-0w level for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL time reflects more time spent at home, which suppresses out-of-home shopping visits and pushes RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises by at least 1.0 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior four-week mean after a one-week increase in RESIDENTIAL of at least 1.0 point.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both strengthen together, commuting and job-linked errands create a multiplicative boost to retail visits, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in TRANSIT below its recent baseline signals tighter movement constraints or weaker commute demand, which reduces spontaneous retail trips and lowers RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -7.0 and stays there for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -5.4 at t-2w and t-1w to -7.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days after TRANSIT remains below -7.0 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: An uptick in PARKS precedes warmer-weather leisure substitution, and that outdoor leisure shift pulls discretionary spending away from retail and recreation venues, lowering RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after PARKS rises by at least 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated while RETAIL_REC remains suppressed, households are reallocating trips toward necessity shopping rather than discretionary shopping, and RETAIL_REC will remain below its last-four-week average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages above its prior four-week mean even though GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above 40 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in TRANSIT after a short rebound indicates renewed mobility friction, and retail activity will weaken with a lag as fewer people combine commuting with shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT reverses and then falls for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks of a two-week TRANSIT downturn.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL and GROCERY_PHARM both stay elevated, people consolidate trips into essentials and avoid discretionary outings, causing RETAIL_REC to drift lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 7 and GROCERY_PHARM remains above 40.
